root_cause.text: The XFS logging subsystem in `xlog_alloc_log` incorrectly defaults the incore log roundoff value (`log->l_iclog_roundoff`) to `BBSIZE` (512 bytes) when the superblock lacks a log stripe unit, failing to account for larger log sector sizes (`mp->m_sb.sb_logsectsize`).
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff in `fs/xfs/xfs_log.c` adds a check `else if (mp->m_sb.sb_logsectsize > 0) log->l_iclog_roundoff = mp->m_sb.sb_logsectsize;` before defaulting to `BBSIZE` in `xlog_alloc_log`, preventing undersized roundoff values on disks with 4k physical sectors.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fall back to the log sector size for log roundoff calculation when logv2 or log stripe units are not in use.
intent_record.what: Added an else-if condition to check if the log sector size is greater than zero and assign it to the log roundoff size.
intent_record.how: Ensures the log roundoff size aligns with the log sector size when logv2 or log stripe units are not active, preventing fallback to the default basic block size.

    xfs: log stripe roundoff is a property of the log
    
    We don't need to look at the xfs_mount and superblock every time we
    need to do an iclog roundoff calculation. The property is fixed for
    the life of the log, so store the roundoff in the log at mount time
